q: What is the purpose of the head office account in a dependent branch's books?

options.A: To track the financial performance of the head office
options.B: To record transactions with the head office
options.C: To calculate the head office's profit
options.D: To manage the head office's expenses

e: Option B (To record transactions with the head office) is the correct choice. In a dependent branch's books, the head office account is the personal account used to record every transaction between the branch and the head office, such as goods sent, cash remitted and expenses paid on the branch's behalf. A dependent branch does not keep full books, so this single account captures the entire branch–head office relationship. A related exam fact: on consolidation, this account exactly cancels out against the branch account in the head office books.

q: What is the primary reason for admitting a new partner to a business?
e: The correct answer is To share profits and losses. The primary reason for admitting a new partner to a business is to share the firm's profits and losses with him, giving him a stake in the business along with the existing partners. Admission also brings fresh capital and expertise into the firm. A related exam fact: on admission, a new partner's profit share is deducted from the old partners' shares in the sacrificing ratio.

q: How is the sacrificing ratio calculated in admission of a new partner?

options.A: New partner's share of profit / Total old partners' share of profit
options.B: Total old partners' share of profit / New partner's share of profit
options.C: New partner's share of profit / Total old and new partners' share of profit
options.D: Total old and new partners' share of profit New partner's share of profit

e: Option A (New partner's share of profit / Total old partners' share of profit) is the correct choice. The sacrificing ratio on the admission of a new partner is calculated as the new partner's share of profit divided by the total share of profit of the old partners, showing what the existing partners give up. It is the ratio in which the old partners surrender a part of their profits in favour of the incoming partner. A related exam fact: goodwill brought in as premium is distributed to the old partners in this sacrificing ratio.

q: What is the maximum number of partners allowed in a partnership firm as per the Companies Act?

A related exam fact: the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 defines a partnership as the relation between persons who agree to share profits carried on by all or any of them. q: In case of the admission of a partner, who has the first right to gain the goodwill of the firm?
e: Option A (Old partners) is the correct choice. Any premium or goodwill raised on admission is therefore credited to the old partners' capital accounts. A related exam fact: the distribution to old partners is made in the sacrificing ratio, which is the old ratio minus the new ratio.

q: What is the formula to calculate hidden goodwill when there is a change in profit-sharing ratio?

options.C: (Change in ratio / Average profit) × Total Capital
